key_insight: PoliVEM unifies multiple virtual element solid-mechanics formulations in one Python-driven framework by reusing a common C++17 core for meshes, projections, assembly, solvers, and boundary handling.
engineering_relevance: It provides a reusable path to implement and compare beam, elasticity, axisymmetric, diffusion, and hyperelasticity models on polygonal/polyhedral meshes with consistent numerical infrastructure.
method: Shared mesh/DOF hierarchy for vertices, edges, faces, and cells
Common energy, strain, and L2 projections with consistency-stabilization split
Modular composition of mesh, material, element, assembler, and solver components
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on polynomial reproduction, patch tests, static condensation recovery, higher-order DOF handling, stiffness spectra, and comparisons with independent finite element calculations.
watch_item: High-order polynomial bases on anisotropic cells and the memory cost of sparse direct factorizations are identified as key implementation limitations.
paper_title: PoliVEM: a Python-driven virtual element framework for computational solid mechanics
